source_documents.title: Anti-Kasha’s Rule Fluorescence Emission in (2-Ferrocenyl)indene Generated by a Twisted Intramolecular Charge-Transfer (TICT) Process

reference_evidence_units.quote: A twisted intramolecular charge-transfer (TICT) process has been identified in (2-ferrocenyl)indene.
This photochemical process explains the anti-Kasha’s rule fluorescence emission observed for this system.
To the best of our knowledge, this is the first example of TICT generated by metal-to-ligand charge transfer (MLCT) in a ferrocene-containing complex
reference_evidence_units.statement: The CT is metal (Fe) to ligand.

structure_verification.problem: two hydrogens missing (C19H14Fe instead of C19H16Fe)
structure_verification.basis: connectivity of the case SMILES kept, hydrogens restored, ionic ferrocene notation
evidence: case SMILES gives C19H14Fe; 2-ferrocenyl-1H-indene is C19H16Fe
the two Fe-bound [c-] atoms carry no H, so each Cp ring lost one H
structure_verification.not_runnable_reason: RDKit ETKDG cannot build a ferrocene sandwich from any SMILES notation tried: the case SMILES embeds as Fe sigma-bonded to two C (Fe-C 1.99 A, others >= 3 A), the ionic notation puts Fe 0.6 A from ring atoms, and eta5 dative bonds fail to embed. The structure-preparation step needs a metallocene template or source geometry; dev runs of 0141 used the sigma-bonded geometry.
